title: No Steps Up to the Altar
kjv_text: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon.
summary: Altars may not be approached by steps, lest the officiant's genitals be exposed beneath his robe while climbing.
original_audience: Altar officiants (pre-Aaronic; later priests get mandatory linen breeches instead, Ex 28:42).
immediate_context: Closes the altar law and the chapter; modesty before God extends to architecture.
historical_context: Ritual nudity was a feature of some ANE cults; Israel legislates against even accidental exposure. The priestly solution evolves: Ex 28:42 mandates underwear, after which Ezekiel's temple vision happily includes altar steps (Ezek 43:17) — a visible dialogue between statute and workaround.
penalty: None stated; for priests, wrongful exposure at the altar risks death (Ex 28:43).
exceptions: Effectively repealed by the breeches mandate (Ex 28:42-43); Ezekiel 43:17 shows a stepped altar.
nt_passages: No direct NT engagement; general modesty texts (1 Timothy 2:9) are the nearest register.

internal_contradictions.issue: No steps (here) vs. Ezekiel's altar with steps (Ezek 43:17) — resolved historically by the breeches mandate, i.e., by underwear.

usofc_implementation: The Sanctuary Architecture Code: all licensed worship platforms must use ramps (grade ≤ 1:12), making the USofC accidentally the world leader in accessible church design — cited constantly, and falsely, as proof the Code is humane. Vestment regulations mandate certified undergarments for all officiants regardless.
constitutional_analogue: Building-code law; its ramp mandate coincidentally reinvents the ADA for altars only.
scene_ideas: A DOW architectural examiner failing a megachurch stage for a 1:11.6 ramp, deadpan, with a laser level.
The Certified Undergarment inspection — the single most despised compliance ritual in the clergy.
satirical_uses: Wheelchair users note the state ramped every altar in the country and not one courthouse door.
